transcript: Last night I was at the first preview of Suffs on Broadway and I thought it was outstanding. It’s about the women's suffrage movement in the United States and the fight to ratify the 19th Amendment for women's right to vote. Already, this was a great premise for musical because the stakes are there. There are a lot of different characters in the show but we centrally follow Alice Paul and her cabinet of activists who are at the forefront of the movement. We see their struggles and sacrifices as well as the debates and tensions that arise within the movement itself around the most effective ways to ignite change. For example, how many demands should your movement be making at once, and when being tactful, how might you be alienating parts of your supporters? I think this show did a great job with showing different aspects of activism and the acknowledgement of how with any major cause, the work is never really done even though progress is possible. I feel like I have to mention that this was a great first preview audience and on my way home, I was kind of questioning whether or not that could have impacted my experience and my opinion of the show. But I've sat for a bit and I've concluded that this is just a really solid musical all around. I didn't see it at the Public, so I went in pretty blind and had no expectations whatsoever but I was really impressed. The pacing is good, the music is lovely (and it advances the plot), and the performances are all around strong and specific. I really couldn't tell you what they're gonna be working on between now and opening night because it already seems so tight. Lastly I just wanted to mention how impressive it is that Shaina Taub who's the composer and lyricist is also starring as Alice Paul. She is setting such a high bar for herself and as far as I can tell, clearing it with flying colors. With that, another playbill for my collection.
reasoning: Tyler expresses strong enthusiasm calling the show 'outstanding' and 'really solid musical all around.' He praises multiple elements including pacing, music, performances, and highlights the impressive dual role of creator/star Shaina Taub.
